title: Animation basics
examples: How many pictures make a smooth animation?
Can I make a movie with just my toys?
What is the difference between stop motion and drawing?

explain.say: Say you know that animation makes things look like they move.
Say this idea is frames per second or fps.
Say stop motion uses physical objects to create animation.
say a flipbook is a book where you draw pictures in order.
say when you combine these ideas you can animate anything.
say think about making a cartoon character wave hello.

faq.q: Why does animation look like it moves?
faq.a: It looks like it moves because you are showing many pictures very quickly one after another. Your brain connects the still pictures to make you see motion.
asks: How does animation trick the eye?
What makes still pictures look alive?

faq.q: What is the difference between stop motion and drawing animation?
faq.a: Stop motion uses real objects that you move between photos. Drawing animation uses drawings that you create on paper or digitally.
asks: Do I need to draw for stop motion?
Is stop motion always with toys?

faq.q: Is a flipbook the same as a movie?
faq.a: A flipbook is like a mini movie you draw yourself. A movie is usually much longer and filmed professionally.
asks: Can I make a movie with a flipbook?
What is the biggest difference between the two?

faq.q: How fast should I take photos for stop motion?
faq.a: You need to take photos slowly enough so that the movement between pictures is small. If you move it too much, it will look jumpy.
asks: Should I move it a little bit each time?
Does the speed matter for stop motion?

faq.q: What is a good frame rate for beginners?
faq.a: Starting with fifteen frames per second is a good place to begin your practice. It will let you see the basic idea of timing.
asks: What is a good starting fps?
Is 12 fps okay to start with?

facts: Animation creates the illusion of movement using rapid sequences of images.
Frames per second measures how many still pictures are shown every second.
Stop motion involves physically manipulating objects between each photograph taken.
A flipbook is a small book designed to show animation by flipping pages quickly.

quiz.say: If you want your animation to look very smooth, should your frames per second be high or low?
quiz.why: A higher frames per second number means more pictures are shown in the same time, making the movement look very smooth.

wrong.0: The number of frames is very important for how smooth the animation appears.
wrong.2: Low fps means you show very few pictures, making the movement look jerky or choppy.
wrong.3: Showing only one picture means there is no movement at all.

quiz.say: What technique uses actual toys or clay figures to create movement?
quiz.why: Stop motion specifically requires you to physically move real objects and photograph them step by step.

wrong.0: Digital animation is done on a computer, not with physical props.
wrong.2: Flipbooks use drawings, not real, movable objects.
wrong.3: Drawing animation requires you to create the image from scratch each time.

quiz.say: If you draw a simple bouncing ball in a book, what are you using?
quiz.why: A flipbook is the perfect tool for showing a sequence of drawings that create the illusion of action.

wrong.0: A graph shows data points, not sequential drawings.
wrong.1: A timeline shows dates in order, not drawings.
wrong.3: Stop motion needs real things you can touch and move.
